definition.simple: A subatomic particle in the nucleus of an atom that has no electrical charge (it is neutral).
definition.academic: A subatomic particle of about the same mass as a proton but without an electric charge, present in all atomic nuclei except those of ordinary hydrogen.

examples: A typical carbon-12 atom has 6 neutrons.
Hydrogen-1 is the only atom that has NO neutrons.

common_misconceptions: Neutrons are totally useless because they have no charge. (False: They are essential for holding the positively charged protons together in the nucleus through the strong nuclear force).
ai_context.tutor_hint: Neutrons are like the 'glue' of the nucleus. Without them, the protons would repel each other and the atom would explode.
